Product API pages (FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator)

Each non-FortiWeb ADOM has its own API page that combines the product's endpoint catalog with a live console; this guide compares them and explains who may run write calls.

👤 ForOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsregistry.view registry.edit registry.execute_write
📍 WhereFortiADC → Automation → API → Registry & console (/adc/api/), FortiAnalyzer → Automation → API → Registry & console (/faz/api/), FortiAuthenticator → Automation → API → Registry & console (/fac/api/)

What these pages are#

Every product ADOM except FortiWeb has its own API page. Each page has two halves:

  • The endpoint catalog — the product's entries in the SATOM endpoint registry (logical name → path or URL), browsed as the product's own menu, with an Other group for entries no menu page uses. This is where you fix a path that moved after a firmware upgrade — no code change is needed.
  • A live console — pick an appliance of that product, a method (or JSON-RPC verb), an endpoint name or raw path and a body, and run it against the device.

The FortiWeb ADOM has the larger API Registry and API Explorer instead; see Endpoint registry. The catalogs are separate per product: a change on one page never affects another product.

Where to find them#

ADOM Page Sidebar entry Who sees the entry
FortiADC FortiADC API-Registry Explorer (/adc/api/) API → Registry & console, below the FortiADC menu groups registry.view
FortiAnalyzer FortiAnalyzer API-Registry Explorer (/faz/api/) API → Registry & console, below the FortiAnalyzer menu groups registry.view
FortiAuthenticator FortiAuthenticator API (/fac/api/) API → Registry & console, below the FortiAuthenticator menu groups registry.view

Opening a page requires registry.view (View registry), and the sidebar entry is shown to exactly the users who hold it. The built-in Viewer, Operator and Administrator profiles all have it. The FortiAuthenticator dashboard and every FortiAuthenticator section page that has tabs also link to it (API console), and FortiAnalyzer panes without an API link to it as API & Registry.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the three API pages require registry.view instead of sign-in alone, and all three sidebars show the same API → Registry & console entry to holders of that permission (FortiADC and FortiAnalyzer used to pin an API link at the bottom for user administrators only, FortiAuthenticator showed it to everyone). The FortiADC and FortiAnalyzer consoles are now dry-run by default like FortiAuthenticator, and all three audit applied writes only. On the FortiAuthenticator page, re-pointing a disabled entry no longer re-enables it, and active entries can be disabled.

Who may do what#

Action FortiADC FortiAnalyzer FortiAuthenticator
Open the page, browse the catalog registry.view registry.view registry.view
Run read calls GET — registry.view get — registry.view GET — registry.view
Run write calls POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE — registry.execute_write exec, add, set, update, delete — registry.execute_write POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE — registry.execute_write
Add, edit, disable, restore catalog entries registry.edit registry.edit registry.edit (add, re-point, disable, restore)
Versions and Reconcile pages registry.edit — —

registry.execute_write (Execute write API calls) is a separate granular permission. It is not part of the built-in Viewer or Operator profiles; the Administrator profile has it. Without it:

  • All three consoles disable the write methods in the selector and the Apply checkbox.
  • FortiADC shows Write methods need the "Execute write API calls" permission., FortiAnalyzer Verbs other than get need the "Execute write API calls" permission. and FortiAuthenticator You may run GET only. Non-GET methods need the Execute write API calls permission.
  • Any write sent anyway is refused with The "Execute write API calls" permission is required for non-GET methods. (FortiAnalyzer: …for non-get verbs.)

Without registry.edit the catalog is read-only: no New Endpoint, edit or disable buttons, and the Disabled panel is not shown.

The three consoles side by side#

FortiADC FortiAnalyzer FortiAuthenticator
Transport REST under /api/… JSON-RPC on one URL; you pick a verb and a url REST under /api/v1/… (Django/Tastypie)
Endpoint field Logical name or raw path starting with / Logical name or raw JSON-RPC url starting with / Logical name or raw path; raw paths must be under /api/v1/
Extra inputs Key Filter (mkey) (appended as ?mkey=), Request Body (JSON), Apply (really write) checkbox Param data (JSON), also allowed on get, Apply (really write) checkbox JSON body (ignored on GET), Apply (really write) checkbox
Writes Dry run by default: the request is shown and nothing is sent until Apply is ticked Dry run by default, as FortiADC Dry run by default, as FortiADC
Status shown The device's HTTP status (HTTP 200) The device's JSON-RPC status code (code 0 on success, ERR <code> with the device error as tooltip) Success or the device error
Reads One request One request Follows pagination to the end
Shortcuts Common paths: version, load_balance_virtual_server, load_balance_pool, system_interface, system_global Common urls: status, device, global, alerts, layout Click any catalog name to fill the endpoint
History Last 20 calls in the page (History, Clear); dry runs are marked DRY Last 20 calls in the page; dry runs are marked DRY —
Audit Applied writes only (adc_api.execute), including the ones the device refused Applied writes only (faz_api.execute), including refused ones Applied writes only (fac_api.execute), including refused ones

Reads and dry runs are not audited. A refused write is recorded with the device's error in the error field.

Using a console#

FortiADC or FortiAnalyzer#

  1. Choose the Appliance.
  2. Pick the method (FortiAnalyzer: the JSON-RPC verb) and type a logical name or a raw path, or click an entry in the API Menu or a common path.
  3. Optionally fill Key Filter (mkey) (FortiADC) and the JSON body (FortiADC: Request Body (JSON); FortiAnalyzer: Param data (JSON)). FortiADC does not send a body with GET or DELETE.
  4. Click Execute Request. The Response panel shows the status badge, the time taken and the highlighted JSON; Copy copies it. FortiADC shows the HTTP status; FortiAnalyzer shows the device's JSON-RPC status code (code 0 means success, ERR <code> means the device refused the call; hover the badge for its error).
  5. For a write (FortiADC: POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE; FortiAnalyzer: any verb other than get), the first Execute Request is a dry run: the badge reads Dry run and the panel shows the method, path and body with Dry run — nothing was sent. Re-submit with Apply to perform this write on the device. Tick Apply (really write), which appears under the method for write methods, and click Execute Request again to send it.

FortiAuthenticator#

  1. Choose the Appliance and the Method.
  2. Type a registry name (for example auth_local_users) or a raw /api/v1/… path, or click a name in Endpoint registry.
  3. For a write, fill JSON body. Leave Apply unticked and click Run: the response shows dry_run: true, the full request and Dry run — nothing was sent. Re-submit with Apply to perform this write on the device.
  4. Tick Apply (really write) and click Run again to send it.

ℹ️Note

POST /api/v1/localusers/ is a bulk endpoint. It answers HTTP 207 with one result per item, and the vendor spells the per-item status key statue. A 2xx answer does not mean every item succeeded — read the body.

Editing the catalog#

FortiADC and FortiAnalyzer#

  1. Click New Endpoint (or + in the API Menu header), or the edit button on an entry.
  2. In Edit Endpoint, fill Logical name, the path (FortiADC: URN / API path; FortiAnalyzer: URN / JSON-RPC url) and API version (v1 for FortiADC, jsonrpc for FortiAnalyzer).
  3. Click Save. The flash reads FortiADC endpoint "…" saved. or FortiAnalyzer endpoint "…" saved.
  4. To disable an entry, click its disable button and confirm Disable endpoint "…"? Services resolving this name will fail loudly until it is restored. Disabled entries move to the Disabled panel, where the restore button (Restore endpoint) brings them back.

FortiAuthenticator#

  1. Under Add or re-point an endpoint, type the logical name and a path under /api/v1/, then click Save. Saving an existing name changes its path and keeps its enabled or disabled state. The flash reads Endpoint … saved., or for a disabled entry Endpoint … saved; it is still disabled — restore it to use it.
  2. To disable an active entry, click the disable button (eye icon, Disable catalog endpoint (soft delete)) next to it and confirm Disable endpoint "…"? Services resolving this name will fail loudly until it is restored.
  3. Disabled entries are listed under Disabled with a Restore button.

All catalog changes are audited (registry.adc_endpoint_create, registry.adc_endpoint_update, registry.adc_endpoint_toggle, registry.faz_endpoint_*, fac_api.registry_save, fac_api.registry_toggle; fac_api.registry_save also records whether the entry is enabled). All three pages save through the same catalog writer, so names, paths and duplicates are checked the same way. The server process that handled the edit drops its catalog cache at once; other server processes refresh theirs within 60 seconds.

Validation messages#

Message Page Meaning
Name and URN are both required. All three One field is empty
Endpoint name may only contain letters, digits, "_", "-" and ".". All three Invalid name
URN must be an absolute API path (e.g. /api/v2.0/cmdb/... or /api/load_balance_pool). FortiADC Path does not start with /
URN must be an absolute JSON-RPC url (e.g. /dvmdb/device). FortiAnalyzer URL does not start with /
An endpoint named "…" already exists (…). FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer Duplicate name for the same API version
URN must be a path under /api/v1/. FortiAuthenticator Path outside the API root

Other sections on these pages#

  • CLI ↔ API coverage — present on all three pages. For FortiADC it compares the configuration tree captured over SSH with the catalog. Reading a CLI block, running it live or capturing a dump needs backups.create or backups.restore. For FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator the section states that no CLI evidence path exists for the product.
  • Versions and Reconcile (FortiADC only, registry.edit) — the firmware-build matrix of the catalog and the sweep results. The Discovery run card points to the API-versions page, where discovery now lives. See Endpoint registry.

Common console errors#

Message Cause What to do
Appliance and endpoint are required. Empty appliance or endpoint Fill both
Selected device is not a FortiADC. / …not a FortiAnalyzer. / …not a FortiAuthenticator. The appliance id belongs to another product Pick a device of this ADOM
Unknown FortiADC endpoint: … / Unknown FortiAnalyzer endpoint: … The logical name is not in the catalog Check the spelling or add the entry
… is not served by … (…) The catalog records that the device's firmware build does not serve that name Use another build or a raw path
Invalid JSON body: … / Body is not valid JSON: … Malformed body Fix the JSON
Invalid endpoint name. FortiAuthenticator logical name with characters other than letters, digits, _, - and . Check the name
Unknown JSON-RPC verb: … / Unknown HTTP method: … Method outside the allowed list (FortiADC and FortiAuthenticator accept GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE); nothing is sent to the device Pick one from the selector
Dry run — nothing was sent. Re-submit with Apply to perform this write on the device. A write was run without Apply (not an error) Tick Apply (really write) and run it again
Raw paths must live under /api/v1/ — the console will not post to the appliance GUI. FortiAuthenticator raw path outside the API Use a /api/v1/… path
405 method not allowed — this resource does not serve that verb … FortiAuthenticator resource that only accepts another method Use the method the resource supports
